issues.t: Vario roof hydraulic cylinders leak
issues.sym: The folding hardtop moves slowly or unevenly, often lower on one side, or stops partway. You may find an oily patch in the trunk, behind the seats or on the headliner, or notice a hydraulic smell on warm days.
issues.why: The roof is moved by several hydraulic cylinders. Their rubber seals harden with age (often after 10 to 15 years) and let fluid leak past. The roof locking cylinder above the windshield is often the first to go and can soak the headliner.
issues.next: Stop using the roof if it is leaking fluid, and don't just top up the reservoir. A roof specialist can reseal the leaking cylinders instead of replacing them.

issues.t: Vario roof hydraulic pump fails
issues.sym: You hear the pump run but the roof doesn't move, the pump runs non-stop, or there is no sound at all when you press the roof switch.
issues.why: The electric hydraulic pump motor behind the passenger seat or in the trunk wears out or seizes with age, especially on cars whose roof is rarely used.
issues.next: Have the roof system scanned before buying a pump, since a bad switch or low fluid can look similar. Use the roof now and then to keep the system healthy.

issues.t: Roof stops mid-cycle from a failed position switch
issues.sym: The roof stops at the same point every time, won't start, or shows a roof or 'visit workshop' warning. The windows and trunk lid may move but the roof does not.
issues.why: The roof only moves when a chain of small switches and sensors confirms the trunk lid, trunk divider, latches and windows are in place. One broken switch or bent actuator arm stops the whole cycle, and scans don't always point to it.
issues.next: Make sure the trunk divider is fully in place and the windows work. Then have a shop read the roof module and test the switches. The fault is often a simple part; most of the work is finding it.

issues.t: Engine stalls or won't restart when hot (crank sensor)
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving and restarts only after it cools down, cranks for a long time before starting, or stalls at idle.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor tells the engine computer where the crankshaft is. When it fails, often from heat, the computer loses the signal and shuts the engine off.
issues.next: If the engine stalls, get safely off the road. Have the codes read; this sensor is a common fix on these cars.

issues.t: Misfire from failing ignition coils
issues.sym: Rough idle (often worse when cold), power loss when accelerating, a check engine light with misfire codes, and sometimes a fuel smell.
issues.why: Ignition coils on these engines wear out with heat and age. The V6 has two spark plugs per cylinder, so tired plugs add strain.
issues.next: Have the codes read to find the weak coil. Shops often replace all coils and plugs together; avoid low-quality no-name coils.

issues.t: No start from failed K40 relay module
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, the fuel pump doesn't prime, or the cooling fans keep running after the car is off.
issues.why: The K40 relay module behind the battery powers several key systems, including the fuel pump. Its solder joints and relays fail with age, mostly on earlier cars.
issues.next: Have the relay module tested. An electronics shop can often resolder it; otherwise replace it.

issues.t: Harsh shifts or stuck in limp mode (5-speed automatic)
issues.sym: Hard 2-3 upshifts, a delay before the car engages Drive or Reverse, or the car stuck in 2nd gear with little power.
issues.why: Speed sensors on the circuit board inside the transmission (the conductor plate) fail with age. Low or old fluid and valve body wear make shifting worse.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned and the fluid level checked. A failed conductor plate can be replaced without a rebuild. Change the fluid about every 40,000 miles.

issues.t: Balance shaft gear wears out
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with camshaft timing codes P0016 or P0017. Early on, the engine runs normally; later you may hear a rattle on startup or feel rough running.
issues.why: On V6 engines built from about 2004 into 2007, the balance shaft sprocket was made from metal that was too soft. Its teeth wear, so the timing chain slips out of step.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a Mercedes dealer whether your engine serial number is in the affected range. Don't put it off: stripped teeth can wreck the engine. Get a firm quote, since it is an engine-out job.

issues.t: Camshaft adjuster magnets leak oil or set codes
issues.sym: A check engine light with camshaft timing codes, rough idle and slow throttle response. You may see oil around the round magnets on the front of the engine.
issues.why: The camshaft adjuster solenoids (magnets) control valve timing. They wear, get clogged by dirty oil, or leak oil out through their connectors.
issues.next: Have the codes read; replacing the magnets is a much smaller job than a balance shaft repair. Check the wiring plugs for oil. Regular oil changes help.

issues.t: Takata driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. The danger is in a crash, when the airbag inflator could burst and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: The driver airbag uses a Takata inflator whose propellant can break down after years of heat and humidity. Mercedes-Benz recalled 2007-2008 SLK280, SLK350 and SLK55 AMG models.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the free driver airbag replacement done at a Mercedes-Benz dealer as soon as possible.

issues.t: Wrong software loaded during service (recall)
issues.sym: Possible loss of drive power, reduced exterior lighting, or loss of stability and traction control.
issues.why: Some control units may have been updated with incorrect software during service visits. Mercedes-Benz recalled many models, including the 2008 SLK350.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the free software check and update done at a dealer.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may switch off for a light adult (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light may come on with a small adult in the seat.
issues.why: The occupant sensing system in the passenger seat of some 2013 SLK250 and SLK350 cars built in late 2012 may mistake a very light adult for a child seat and turn the airbag off.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the passenger seat cushion with its sensor for free.

issues.t: Front passenger airbag may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. The problem only shows in a crash.
issues.why: An assembly error on some 2014 SLK250, SLK350 and SLK55 AMG cars built between March and May 2014 could keep the passenger airbag from deploying correctly, and a loose part could enter the cabin.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Until it is fixed, keep people and items off the front passenger seat. The dealer replaces the airbag for free.

issues.t: Emergency call system may send the wrong location (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in daily driving. The fault only matters if the car's emergency call (eCall) system is used.
issues.why: A software fault can make the emergency call system's clock wrong, so it may send an inaccurate location to emergency responders.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. The fix is a free software update, done over the air or at a dealer.

issues.t: Stability control may leave the brakes partly on (recall)
issues.sym: After a stability control intervention, the car may keep slowing down as if the brakes were dragging, and the brakes can overheat.
issues.why: A software fault in the stability control system could keep some brake pressure applied. Mercedes-Benz recalled certain 2015 SLK250, 2016 SLK350 and later SLC models.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the free software update done. If the car drags or the brakes smell hot, stop safely and call a dealer.

issues.t: Low-beam headlights aimed wrong from the factory (recall)
issues.sym: Poor night visibility or other drivers flashing their lights at you.
issues.why: On some 2016 SLK300 and SLK350 cars built in summer 2015, the low beams may have been aimed incorrectly at the factory.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. The dealer adjusts the headlight aim for free.

issues.t: Body rust on older roadsters
issues.sym: Rust bubbles around wheel arches, door bottoms, sills and trunk edges, and corrosion around the subframe mounts underneath.
issues.why: Cars of this era used water-based paint and were not galvanized, so road salt and trapped water cause rust.
issues.next: Have the body and underside checked, especially in snowy or wet climates. Fix rust early before it spreads to structural parts.

issues.t: Retractable hardtop leaks or won't work properly
issues.sym: Water getting into the cabin, wind noise, or a roof that is slow, noisy or stops partway.
issues.why: The folding hardtop relies on seals, sensors and hydraulic parts that wear with age and use. Owners call a leaking or faulty top the main thing to check on these cars.
issues.next: Test the roof through several full cycles and look for damp carpets before buying. Have a roof specialist diagnose problems before they get worse.

issues.t: Rattle on startup from camshaft adjuster wear
issues.sym: A rattle for a few seconds after starting, rough idle, uneven running and a check engine light with camshaft timing codes.
issues.why: The camshaft adjuster gear can wear against the timing chain. Left alone, the chain stretches and the valve timing drifts, which in the worst case lets valves and pistons hit.
issues.next: Don't ignore a startup rattle. Have the timing codes read and the chain and adjusters inspected. Fixing it early can prevent a damaged engine.

issues.t: Rattle for a few seconds after starting
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine for a few seconds right after a start, then it goes quiet.
issues.why: Oil pressure in the secondary timing chain tensioners drops while the car sits. Mercedes issued a service bulletin and said no lasting damage was expected.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer about the service bulletin, which replaces the secondary chain tensioners and adds check valves in the cylinder heads.
